Consult Summary:
- Acute new, persistent headache for three days with photophobia and impaired concentration/work capacity; evaluation planned with neurological and eye examination, and treatment initiated with a stronger NSAID plus paracetamol; contraception review and follow-up arrangements discussed.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Blinding headache started three days ago, persistent and affecting ability to work and concentrate.
  - Pain described as all over with stronger sensation around the right eye.
  - Photophobia present; occasional “weird” visual phenomena (shooting light); no nausea or vomiting reported.
- Timeline and progression:
  - Woke with headache three days ago; has been continuous with partial relief from ibuprofen but not resolution.
  - Ibuprofen provides some relief but symptoms persist.
  - Sleep intact; no nighttime awakening due to headache.
  - Pain severity reported as about 8/10 at worst, down to ~5-6/10 with some relief.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Standing up quickly may provoke a stabbing pain.
  - Head movement may produce a sensation of something moving inside.
  - Ibuprofen provides partial relief but does not fully relieve symptoms.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Light sensitivity (photophobia).
  - Visual disturbances described as brief flashes or “weird” vision.
  - No fever, cough, sore throat, sinus symptoms, nasal bleeding, or coughing up blood.
  - No numbness or weakness reported.
  - No weight change noted; slight fatigue/low energy potentially related to pain.
- Past medical history:
  - Prior headaches in childhood/adolescence described as brief and not causing persistent symptoms; one previous headache episode lasting about two days that resolved with ibuprofen.
  - No other significant medical problems reported.
- Medications:
  - Oral contraceptive pill started about a year ago (name not specified).
  - Ibuprofen used for headaches; dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Paracetamol not currently used but discussed as safe to co-administer.
- Allergies:
  - None reported.
- Social history:
  - Lives alone.
  - Non-smoker.
  - Alcohol: about three drinks per week.
  - Works from home; has occasionally taken days off due to headaches.
- Family history:
  - Mother has migraines with vomiting (noted as a family history of migraines).

Past Medical History (summary):
- Headache history: single prior mild headache in childhood; similar episodes in the past not previously severe.
- Contraceptive pill use for ~1 year.
- No other chronic conditions or allergies reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical exam findings: Not documented.
- Additional notes: Eye exam reportedly recently performed with no vision changes detected at that time.

Investigations:
- Planned during visit:
  - Neurological examination (full exam).
  - Ophthalmologic examination focusing on the back of the eyes (fundoscopy/retina).
  - Blood pressure assessment at the examination.
- Current results: None documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute new headache with features suggesting possible migraine; ongoing for three days with photophobia and transient visual phenomena.
  - Plan:
    - Schedule a full neurological examination and ophthalmologic eye examination (including assessment of the back of the eyes).
    - Start a stronger NSAID alternative to ibuprofen and continue/paracetamol as well; medications to be prescribed:
      - Stronger NSAID (name not specified) — dose/route/frequency not documented; take with food.
      - Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented; take as advised with the NSAID.
    - Blood pressure measurement at the appointment to assess suitability of the current oral contraceptive pill.
    - Review and potential adjustment of the oral contraceptive pill if migraines with flashing lights occur; discuss suitability and possible changes if migraine features persist.
    - Consider referral to a specialist; arrangement to be made via the support team after the initial examination.
    - If symptoms worsen, change, or you develop new red flag symptoms (e.g., fever, severe neck stiffness, focal neurological deficits, rapidly progressing headache), seek urgent care (A&E).
    - Follow-up: If headache settles, the planned appointment can be canceled.

General plan items:
- Take prescribed stronger NSAID with food; use paracetamol as needed alongside.
- Attend scheduled neurological and eye examinations; have blood pressure checked during visit.
- Reassess migraine vs other etiologies; adjust contraception if migraine with aura/visual disturbances persist.
- Contact support line for referral scheduling and additional advice as needed.

  - Current medication list reconciliation with doses, routes, and frequencies for ibuprofen and the pill.
  - Lab tests or imaging results not available; none discussed beyond planned examinations.
- Internal conflicts:
  - No clear conflicts identified in the transcript.

  - Some portions are ambiguous (e.g., exact pill name, precise NSAID suggested) and certain details (dosages) are not documented; overall the plan is consistent with the information given.
